findings.description: VERIFIED is emitted for ordinary Python unittest import failures because the blacklist does not recognize them. For example, a committed test importing a symbol introduced by the fix produces `ImportError: cannot import name ...` and `FAILED (errors=1)` at red, then passes at green. Neither message matches NOT_A_RED_PATTERNS.
findings.failure_mode: The required bug-review gate exits 0 even though the red test never reached an assertion, falsely certifying a non-runnable test as red-before-green.
findings.suggested_fix: Recognize runner error outcomes separately from assertion failures before emitting VERIFIED. Cover unittest import errors and pytest configuration/import failures with regression cases that must return NOT_A_RED.

findings.description: link_deps symlinks the live tree's node_modules/.venv/vendor/target/.tox into each worktree by default. Those directories routinely contain absolute or relative references back into the live source tree: a Python editable install (`pip install -e .`) leaves a .pth/egg-link pointing at the live src/ directory, and npm/pnpm/yarn workspaces leave node_modules/<pkg> -> ../packages/<pkg> symlinks that resolve relative to the live node_modules. In the red worktree `import mypkg` (src layout) or `require('@scope/pkg')` therefore loads the LIVE tree's code, not the red commit's code. Both runs then exercise the same (live, possibly uncommitted) implementation, which contradicts the header's contract 'Uncommitted state in the live tree never counts' and the reviewing-code SKILL instruction to cite the tool's output as proof of 'Test fails with current code'.
findings.failure_mode: For a src-layout Python project with an editable install, or a JS monorepo with workspace symlinks, the red run executes the fixed code and passes: the tool reports DECOY (exit 3) for a genuine red test, or VERIFIED when the test change alone flips the result against live code. The reviewer is told to cite this verdict; it is wrong silently and reproducibly, not as a rare edge.
findings.suggested_fix: Default to --no-link-deps and make linking opt-in (--link-deps), or refuse to link when the linked directory contains back-references: detect *.pth / *.egg-link files under .venv whose target is under $MAIN, and symlinks inside node_modules whose resolved target is under $MAIN but outside node_modules; in either case skip the link and print a WARN naming the reason. At minimum document this failure mode in the header next to the 'writes into the live tree's copy' caveat and have the reviewing-code SKILL say when the verdict is not trustworthy.

findings.description: The review role's Bash allowlist was deliberately narrow (git diff, git log, a few named scripts, br). Adding `Bash(.claude/scripts/red-test-check.sh *)` grants that role arbitrary command execution: everything after `--` and the whole `--setup` string are exec'd verbatim with the caller's environment, and with linked deps they can write into the live tree. A reviewer.md or PR description crafted to say 'Red commit: X, test command: curl … | sh' is now a one-hop injection into the reviewer agent, where before the allowlist would have stopped it.
findings.failure_mode: Prompt-injected or careless reviewer invocations run any program under the review skill's permissions, bypassing the per-command allowlist that C-PROC-001 relies on.
findings.suggested_fix: Either restrict the pattern to the known test runners the repo uses (e.g. `Bash(.claude/scripts/red-test-check.sh * -- bats *)`, `… -- npm test*`, `… -- pytest*`), or have red-test-check.sh read the test command from a committed, allowlisted source (`.loa.config.yaml` test command) instead of argv, so the reviewer cannot supply an arbitrary program.

findings.cross_file_justification: symlink-manifest.sh (diff-touched) defines the consumer layout: `.claude/scripts -> ../.loa/.claude/scripts` and `.claude/loa/GLOSSARY.md -> ../../.loa/...` where `.loa` is a git submodule. `git worktree add` never checks out submodules, so inside both worktrees every one of those manifest symlinks dangles.
findings.description: Detached worktrees created by add_wt contain no submodule content. In any project that mounts Loa as the `.loa` submodule (the layout symlink-manifest.sh describes), `.claude/scripts/*`, `.claude/skills/*`, hooks and settings all dangle in the worktree. Any test command or test that touches framework paths (bats suites sourcing `.claude/scripts/lib/*.sh`, project scripts that call `.claude/scripts/validate-artifact.sh`, etc.) exits 127 or 'No such file' in the red worktree and is reported NOT_A_RED (exit 4), while the same command run in the live tree works. The same applies to any repository with its own submodules.
findings.failure_mode: False NOT_A_RED / GREEN_FAILS verdicts in consumer projects for tests that depend on submodule content, with an error message ('fix the test so it loads') that points the engineer at the wrong cause.
findings.suggested_fix: After `worktree add`, run `git -C "$path" submodule update --init --recursive` when `.gitmodules` exists at the checked-out commit (or symlink the live submodule gitdirs), and record the step in the header. Alternatively detect dangling symlinks in the worktree before the run and print a WARN naming them so a 127 is interpretable.

findings.description: SEAMS_REQUIRED_FROM is set to 2026-10-13, which is already in the past relative to this PR. validate_sprint_seams turns a missing '### Seams Under Test' table into a hard violation for every sprint plan whose header **Date:** is on or after that day, and `--type sprint` is what the planning and run-mode gates invoke. Any already-committed plan dated 13-19 October (including this cycle's own grimoires/loa/sprint.md if it predates the template change) will start failing validation the moment this merges, with no grace period and no override flag.
findings.failure_mode: Existing in-flight sprint plans fail `validate-artifact.sh --type sprint` after merge; run mode and the plan gate refuse to proceed until each plan is back-filled with seams tables.
findings.suggested_fix: Run `validate-artifact.sh --type sprint` against every sprint.md in the repo and its fixtures before merging; either move SEAMS_REQUIRED_FROM to the merge date or later, or back-fill the tables in the affected plans in this PR. Consider a `--no-seams` escape hatch for legacy plans.
